translations.text: Another king rose to power over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
Because the midwives feared God, they built houses.
Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Throw every boy born to the Hebrews into the Nile, but keep every girl alive.”
When they could no longer hide him, his mother took a basket and coated it with bitumen and pitch. She put the child inside it and placed it among the reeds beside the Nile.
His sister watched from a distance to find out what would happen to him.
The child’s sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Would you like me to call a nursing woman from among the Hebrew women to nurse this child for you?”
The priest of Midian had seven daughters, who tended their father’s sheep. When they came, they drew [?] until they filled the troughs to water their father’s sheep.
He said to his daughters, “Where is he? Why did you leave the man like that? Call him so that he may eat some food.”
Moses said to God, “Look, I will go to the Israelites and tell them, ‘The God of your ancestors has sent me to you.’ If they ask me his name, what shall I tell them?”
The Lord said to Moses, “What is this in your hand?” He said, “A staff.”
“Now go, and I will open your mouth and teach you what you must say.”
Zipporah took a razor and cut off her son’s foreskin. She fell at his feet and said, “Let this blood from my son’s circumcision be a substitute for him.”
Aaron told them all the words that God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
Their taskmasters kept urging them on, saying, “Complete your work each day, just as when we gave you straw.”
They met Moses and Aaron as they were coming out from Pharaoh.
“Go in and tell Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to send the Israelites out of his land.”
These are the messengers, according to their ancestral houses:
The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I have made you a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.”
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded them. Aaron raised his staff and struck the water in the Nile before Pharaoh and his officials, and the water in the Nile became blood.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the Lord says: Let my people go so that they may serve me (in the wilderness).’”
Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought out the frogs. The frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh and cried out to the Lord for the destruction of the frogs, as Pharaoh had requested.
They gathered them into heaps, and the land stank.
When Pharaoh saw that there was relief, his heart became hard, and he refused to listen to them, as the Lord had said.
The Lord said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out the staff in your hand and strike the dust of the ground, and gnats will come out upon people and animals throughout the land of Egypt.’”
And the Lord did so. Dogflies came in great numbers into Pharaoh’s houses, into the houses of his officials, and throughout the land of Egypt. The land was ruined by the dogflies.
We will go three days’ journey into the open country and sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he told us.
But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also and refused to let the people go.
It will become dust throughout the land of Egypt, and it will cause boils that break out on people and animals, on human beings and four-footed creatures throughout the land of Egypt.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let hail fall throughout the land of Egypt, on people, on animals, and on all the vegetation in the land.”
But the wheat and peas were not struck, because they were ripe.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, so that my signs may come upon them together.”
And they summoned Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh, and he said to them (Pharaoh to Moses and Aaron), “Go and serve the Lord your God. But who exactly are those of you who will go?”
And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and darkness and dust covered the whole land of Egypt for three days.
And Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, “Go and serve the Lord your God, but leave your sheep and cattle behind. You may take your possessions with you.”

Our livestock must also go with us, and we will leave nothing behind, because we will take some of them to sacrifice to the Lord our God. We do not know what service we must render to the Lord our God until we arrive there.
This month shall be the first of the months for you; put it before the other months of the year.

Take a bundle of hyssop and dip it in the blood beside the door. Apply some of that blood beside the door of the house to the lintel and both doorposts. And you must not leave that house until morning.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the law of the Passover: no one of a foreign people may eat of it.”
And on that day the Lord brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt with their forces.
And the Lord said to Moses:
And the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites to turn back and camp opposite Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, toward Baal-zephon. Camp opposite them, beside the sea.”
And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them. I will be glorified through Pharaoh and all his army, and all Egypt will know that I am the Lord.

And the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled. Pharaoh’s heart and the hearts of his officials turned against the people, and he said, “What have we done, letting the Israelites go so that they no longer serve us?”

And they said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in the land of Egypt that you brought us out to kill us in the wilderness? What have you done to us by bringing us out of the land of Egypt?”
The Lord will fight for you, and you must remain silent.
And you led your people whom you redeemed; by your strength you made the remnant of your sanctuary rejoice.
The nations heard and trembled; anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
At that time the chiefs of Edom trembled; shaking seized the messengers of Moab, and all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
Fear and trembling seized them; the strength of your arm was greater than rocks, until your people passed over, Lord, until your people passed over—this people whom you redeemed.
Miriam took the lead and said, “Let us bless the Lord. He is wonderful, wonderful! He threw the horse and its rider into the sea.”
Moses cried out to the Creator, and the Lord showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There he showed him righteousness and judgment, and tested him.

Moses said, “In the evening the Lord will give you meat to eat, and in the morning bread until you are satisfied, because the Lord has heard your grumbling—the grumbling with which you grumble against us. And who are we? This grumbling of yours is not against us, but against the Creator.”

“I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘In the evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the Lord, your Creator.’”
They gathered it every morning, each for himself, and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On Friday they gathered a double portion, two omers for each person. All the leaders of the assembly came and told Moses.
Moses said to them, “Eat it today, because today is the Lord’s Sabbath. You will not find it in the wilderness.”
On the seventh day, some of the people went out to gather it, but found none.

Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took an offering and made a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness. Aaron and the leaders of the people of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before the Lord.
Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek judgment from the Lord.”
In the third month after the Israelites left the land of Egypt, on that day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet the Creator, and they reached the mountain.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people not to approach the Lord to look at him, lest many among them fall.”
Honor your father and your mother, so that righteousness may be yours. You will have many days in the righteous land that the Lord God gives you.
Do not worship gods of silver, and do not worship gods of gold. Do not make such gods for yourselves.
If you acquire a Jewish slave, keep him for seven years, and in the seventh year set him free without payment.
If someone has stolen among the Israelites, and [?] your companion [?] you bring back [?], whoever you find shall be sentenced to death.
If someone wounds his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies, the one who inflicted the wound shall surely be put to death.
If two men fight and injure a pregnant woman, and she miscarries and there is no human form, they shall fine him if her husband agrees to a settlement, according to his demand.
If she miscarries when it is formed, he shall pay life for life.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.
If he breaks a molar or tooth of his male or female slave, he shall set them free in compensation for their tooth.
Whether it is a male slave or a female slave, he shall give thirty pieces of silver to the slave’s owner in either case, and his ox shall be stoned.
Do not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, because you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall be holy people to me. Do not eat the flesh of an animal killed by a wild beast; throw it to the dogs.
Keep away from every unjust judgment. Do not kill the innocent and the righteous, and do not spare the guilty.
For seven years sow your fields and gather your harvest.
But in every seventh year leave it to rest, so that the poor of your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what remains. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.
Observe everything I have said. Do not mention the names of gods, and do not speak them with your mouths.
Three times every male shall appear before me, the Lord your God.
Bring the first fruits of your fields into the house of the Lord your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
I will not drive them out in a single year, so that the land does not become desolate and the wild animals of the land do not multiply against you.
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Moses rose early in the morning and built an altar beside the mountain, and twelve stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you stone tablets bearing the law and the commandment that I have written, so that you may instruct them.”
The splendor of the Lord descended upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
Insert its poles into those four rings on the supports of the ark, as carrying poles for the ark by which they will carry it.
Make a covering of pure gold to fit above it, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Place the covering on top of the ark, and put inside the ark the commandment that I will give you.
Make its dishes, its bowls, its pouring vessels, and its measuring vessels with which you will pour. Make them of pure gold.
Place bread on the table before me continually.
For the shaft of the lampstand, make four cups, with its flowers and its rounded tops.
Fashion what is behind it and its arrangement [?] from pure gold.
Five curtains shall be joined, one joined to another, and five curtains shall be linked to one another.
Make fifty loops along the edge of one curtain, at the middle where the curtains are joined. Make fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain, where it is joined to the first.
Each upright shall be ten cubits high and one and a half cubits wide.
Make forty silver sockets for the twenty uprights: two sockets for one upright, for its two faces, and two sockets for another upright, for its two faces.
Make for it pans for the sacrifices, its shovels, its bowls, its meat forks, and its fire pans. Make them all of bronze.
Its boards shall be hollow. Make it that way, just as I showed you on the mountain; make it that way.
On the other side, the curtain shall stand fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.
With the work of a skilled craftsman, engrave both stones with the names of the sons of Israel, as a seal is engraved.
And you shall make wild animals of the earth from pure gold.
And it shall be set with settings, with its stones in four rows. A row of stones shall be made of sardius, topaz, and emerald: one row.
And you shall place it opposite where the hooks of its chain project [judgment], on both sides, from its shoulder pieces; and you shall place it from the judgment [?].

And above it and below it you shall make things like pomegranate fruit, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, below the woven garment, all around it. Join it [?] to golden pomegranates, with bells between them all around.
And the golden pomegranates, their bells, and their flowers shall be at the [?] of his garment all around.
And you shall put it on a blue thread, and they shall place it on the serpent, so that it rests at the end of the serpent.
And you shall cut it into its separate pieces, wash its entrails and its legs, and place its head among the pieces you have cut.
And you shall offer the whole ram on the altar as an offering to the Lord.
And you shall take it from their hands and offer it on the altar as a pleasing aroma before the Lord. It is an offering to the Lord.
And you shall take the breast of the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and present it as a special offering before the Lord, and it alone shall be your portion.

And it shall be a perpetual ordinance for Aaron and his sons among the Israelites, because this is a special offering. It shall be a special offering from the Israelites, from the sacrifices they offer for their deliverance, a special offering to the Lord.
And you shall take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might be called upon by them and be their God.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold—its base, its sides all around, and its horns—and you shall make a gold molding around it.
Look, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
And I have provided Eliab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. And I have given understanding to everyone skilled in heart, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
And the oil used for anointing and the incense burned for the sanctuary. And they shall make everything I command you.
And keep my Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Whoever profanes it shall certainly be put to death. Whoever does work on it—that person shall be cut off from their people.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall certainly [?] be put to death.
And all the people took off the earrings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
And now leave me alone, and in my anger and wrath I will destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.

And he said to them, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Let each man carry his sword. Go from gate to gate through the camp, and let each man kill his brother, let each man kill his fellow, and let each man kill his neighbor.”
And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them, and three thousand men from among the people fell at that time.
And on the next day Moses said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. And now I will go up to the Lord to obtain forgiveness for your sin.”
And the Lord killed some of the people because they had made the calf that Aaron made for them.
And God said to Moses, “Here is a place beside me, and you shall stand on the rock.”
“Be ready in the morning, and go up Mount Sinai. Stand there before me on the mountaintop.”
And the Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, merciful and compassionate, slow to anger, abundant in mercy, and righteous,

who preserves righteousness and shows mercy to thousands, who forgives wrongdoing, error, and sin, but does not acquit the guilty; who brings the fathers’ sins upon their children and their children’s children, to the third and fourth generation.”
And Moses said, “If I have found favor before you, let my Lord go with us, for this people is stubborn. Forgive the sin and guilt of your people, and we will belong to you.”
“You shall celebrate the Sabbath festival for me when the wheat harvest begins, and the Festival of Booths in the middle of the year.”
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and saw that his face had become radiant, they were afraid to approach him.
And the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, and the altar and all its utensils;
and the garments of Aaron the priest, and the garments in which they serve in the sanctuary;
Everyone who had pledged an offering of silver or bronze brought an offering to God. Everyone who had wood that does not decay brought it for all the work needed for the tabernacle.
And all the women whose hearts prompted them skillfully spun the goats’ hair.
And they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more offerings than are needed for the work that God commanded to be done.”
And all the skilled workers who made the sacred garments made them for Aaron the priest, as God had commanded Moses.
They cut the gold leaf and made it into threads to be woven with blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver.
And they made two twisted circlets and two gold rings.

He fastened the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod. They were secured with blue cords and woven into the [?] of the ephod, so that the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as God had commanded Moses.
And they made linen tunics, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons;
and they made an embroidered curtain for the doorway of the tabernacle, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and twisted fine linen, the work of a weaver, and depicted cherubim on it.
And its five pillars, their rings, their capitals, and their bands they overlaid with gold; and their five bases were of bronze.
And the courtyard on the west side was fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and ten bases.
And the hanging on the south side was fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
And its four pillars had four bronze bases. Their fastenings were of silver, their capitals were covered with silver, and the pillars themselves were covered with silver.
Handles by which they grasp it when they lift it.
And he made carrying poles for the ark and the table and covered them with gold.
One hundred talents for one hundred capitals; one talent for each capital.
The bronze from the offering amounted to four hundred and seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
Moses saw all the work that had been done. They had done it just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Moses blessed them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
You shall put the ark of the testimony in place and screen the ark with the curtain.
You shall place the golden incense altar, on which incense is burned, before the ark of the testimony, and put a curtain at the entrance of the tent of the testimony.
He arranged its lamps before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the golden incense altar in the tent of the testimony, in front of the curtain.
